info.title: Yogabase Builds API
info.description: Send one build archive, ask what the checks found, ask again. Yogabase derives the service layout and the software inventory from the archive itself, and the member's isolated admission Job derives the security scan; a producer that already signs may pass its own manifest through unchanged. Two credentials reach these routes and no third: the console session of a signed-in seat with project-management permission, and a project-scoped developer token. The workload delivery bearer is deliberately not accepted.

controlPlaneHost.description: The installation's own Control Plane origin.

post.summary: Upload one build archive and start its checks.
post.description: The bundle is the only part every upload needs. For a self-contained service, every field beside it is a hint, needed only where the archive is genuinely ambiguous: which executable to launch when more than one is present, and which ports it listens on. Absent hints are derived — the executable from the single root ELF or the Unity player, the architecture from that ELF's machine type, the name from the executable, the version from a fixed default, and the ports from one UDP listener on 7777. A Lambda archive must also state how it runs, because Yogabase never derives it: executionKind, realtimeIngressBindings and realtimeEgressBindings. Yogabase writes them into the manifest it derives. A Lambda upload without all three is refused with 400 BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_REQUIRED naming the missing field, before anything is recorded; an unknown kind is BUILD_LAMBDA_EXECUTION_KIND_INVALID, a malformed binding id BUILD_LAMBDA_BINDING_INVALID (the field names its position, e.g. realtimeEgressBindings[1]), a repeated one BUILD_LAMBDA_BINDING_DUPLICATE, and more than 16 in one direction BUILD_LAMBDA_BINDINGS_TOO_MANY. The three fields sent for a self-contained service are refused with BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_UNEXPECTED. With a signed manifest, the manifest's own executionDeclaration is the declaration: a Lambda manifest without one is refused with BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_REQUIRED (field manifest.executionDeclaration), one a member would not admit with BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_INVALID, and the three fields sent beside a manifest with BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_CONFLICT. A Lambda archive whose entry is RegisterLambdas registers several Lambda ids, which are known only once its code runs; it states them in registeredLambdaIds and Yogabase writes them into the derived manifest as its registration, each of the one kind the execution kind allows (Stateless registers functions, Stateful actor handlers). A registering archive without them is refused with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_REQUIRED, the field sent for a single-function (InvokeAsync) archive with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_UNEXPECTED, a malformed id with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_ID_INVALID and a repeated one, or one equal to the build's own name, with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_ID_DUPLICATE (the field names its position, e.g. registeredLambdaIds[2]), more than 64 with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_TOO_MANY, and a realtime ingress binding that is not a registered id with BUILD_LAMBDA_REGISTRATION_BINDING_UNBOUND; the field sent beside a signed manifest is BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_CONFLICT, and a signed manifest's own registration a member would not admit is BUILD_LAMBDA_DECLARATION_INVALID (field manifest.registration). A Lambda admitted from the manifest Yogabase derived is unsigned: it resolves at invocation on this installation's own admission attestation, with no registered signer.

manifest.description: Optional detached signed manifest, passed through unchanged.

executable.description: Archive-relative path of the process to launch.

ports.description: Repeatable port declarations in the name=7777/udp spelling.

executionKind.description: Required for a Lambda archive uploaded without a manifest; refused for a self-contained service. Stateless keeps no state between calls; Stateful keeps durable state per actor. Spelled exactly as listed.

realtimeIngressBindings.description: Required for a Lambda archive uploaded without a manifest; refused for a self-contained service. Comma-separated realtime binding ids the Lambda receives events from. Send the field empty to declare none; an absent field is not a declaration. Each id starts with a lowercase letter and uses only lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 96 characters; at most 16 ids, each once. Repeated parts are combined.

realtimeEgressBindings.description: Required for a Lambda archive uploaded without a manifest; refused for a self-contained service. Comma-separated realtime binding ids the Lambda publishes events to; it can publish only to these. The same rules as realtimeIngressBindings, including an empty field to declare none.

registeredLambdaIds.description: Required for a Lambda archive whose entry is RegisterLambdas uploaded without a manifest; refused for a single-function (InvokeAsync) archive, for a self-contained service, and beside a signed manifest. Comma-separated Lambda ids the bundle registers: each starts with a lowercase letter and uses only lowercase letters, digits, '.', '_' and '-', at most 128 characters, compared ordinally and never case-folded; 1 to 64 ids, each once and none equal to the build's own name. Every realtime binding the Lambda receives must be one of these ids. The sandbox verifies, before any id is served, that the bundle registers exactly these ids. Repeated parts are combined.

202.description: The build is recorded and its checks are queued.

get.summary: Read one build and what its checks found.

post.summary: Run the checks again for the same bytes.
post.description: The digest never changes, so this is a re-check of one build rather than a new one: the case it exists for is a build refused by a vulnerability database that has since moved on, or by a dependency that was briefly unavailable.

developerToken.description: A project-scoped developer token, issued from the console's Settings page and prefixed 'ybt_'. It carries the builds:write and/or builds:read scope and has no authority outside its own project's builds. Yogabase stores only its SHA-256, so a lost token is revoked and reissued rather than recovered.

consoleSession.name: __Host-Yogabase
consoleSession.description: The signed-in console seat's session. It must carry project-management permission.

Refused.description: The request was refused. The problem names the field a person can correct.

ScopeRequired.description: The developer token does not carry the scope this verb needs.

NotFound.description: No such build in this environment. A developer token scoped to another project receives this rather than a forbidden, so it cannot be used to discover which project ids exist.

identity.description: The build's own identity and version, as functionId:version or serviceId:version.

attempt.description: Which upload of this identity this is, starting at 1. A corrected re-upload takes the next attempt and supersedes the refused one.

evidenceOrigin.description: Whether the inventory and scan came with the build or were derived from it.

databaseDigest.description: Digest of the vulnerability snapshot the scan was matched against, when reported.

passed.description: False until the checks report. An absent result is never reported as a clean one.

id.description: The advisory identifier, e.g. a CVE or GHSA id.

version.description: The version present in the build.

fixedIn.description: First fixed version, or empty when none is published.

entry.description: The archive entry the component was catalogued from.

field.description: The field the refusal is about, or empty.

cause.description: A bounded cause token, never a message or a value.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem details, extended with a stable machine 'code' and the correlation id.
